The core issue lies in how de-vigging adapters handle asymmetric inputs. Prior to fix (#965), the adapter incorrectly labeled all computed vectors as additive regardless of actual method. This led to inconsistent outputs like `homeFair` being negative, violating probability axioms. Asymmetric tests expose this by comparing expected vs computed values. For example, `-110/-125` should yield `homeFair=0.4853`, but old code returned incorrect values due to zero-division or mislabeling. The new tests enforce correctness through validation of both output structure and method semantics. The multiplicative model correctly normalizes odds into fair probabilities, whereas the additive version adjusts differently. Zero inputs are rejected outright to prevent undefined behavior. These primitives form a dual system where each adapter ensures internal consistency and external compatibility with probabilistic models.
